seoTitle: Using MT4 Indicators in TradingView: What's Possible
metaDescription: Learn what happens when switching from MT4 to TradingView, how to find similar indicators, use Pine Script alternatives, and avoid common mistakes.
intro: Traders moving from MetaTrader 4 to TradingView often want to keep using their favorite MT4 indicators, but the two platforms don't work identically. This guide explains what's actually possible when trying to replicate MT4 indicators, how to search for similar tools in TradingView, and how Pine Script alternatives can fill the gap. It's aimed at forex traders making the switch between platforms.

steps.heading: Understand MT4 vs TradingView differences
steps.body: MT4 indicators are typically written in MQL4, while TradingView uses Pine Script, so indicators can't be directly imported between the two platforms.

steps.heading: Search for similar MT4-style indicators
steps.body: Browse TradingView's public library for indicators with similar names or functionality to the ones you used on MT4.

steps.heading: Use Pine Script alternatives
steps.body: Look for community-built Pine Script versions that replicate the logic of popular MT4 indicators.

steps.heading: Copy logic and recreate indicators if needed
steps.body: If you can't find a direct match, understanding the original indicator's logic can help you or a developer recreate it in Pine Script.

steps.heading: Watch for common mistakes when switching platforms
steps.body: Be aware that even similarly named indicators can calculate slightly differently between MT4 and TradingView, so verify results before relying on them.

faq.question: Can I directly import an MT4 indicator into TradingView?
faq.answer: No, MT4 indicators are written in a different language than TradingView's Pine Script, so they can't be imported directly without being recreated.

faq.question: Are there Pine Script versions of popular MT4 indicators?
faq.answer: Many popular MT4-style indicators have community-created Pine Script equivalents available in TradingView's public script library.

faq.question: Will a Pine Script alternative calculate exactly the same as the original MT4 indicator?
faq.answer: Not always; even similarly named indicators can have slight calculation differences, so it's worth comparing results before relying on them fully.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to code to recreate an MT4 indicator?
faq.answer: Recreating an indicator from scratch generally requires some Pine Script knowledge, though many common indicators already have existing versions you can use instead.
